scope: Isolated S1 failures of a child frame whose navigation waits for its response headers, and process loss of a parsing sandboxed srcdoc child. Three shared cases unwind the event loop of a child frame's pending pipeline: a same-site pipeline in the parent's event loop, a cross-site pipeline in a child-site popup's event loop, and a cross-site pipeline alone in a new event loop. Six multiprocess cases exit or kill the process of the pending pipeline in each layout. Two multiprocess cases exit or kill the process of the parsing sandboxed srcdoc child. The engine patch adds only probe messages and methods that target the view's newest pending child-frame pipeline. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: A failed buffer shows a native, platform-styled error state until the user recovers or kills it (2026-11-24).
An error page is recoverable by navigating back, reloading, or editing the target URL (2026-11-24).

baseline.head: ffac748
baseline.note: The cross-site parsing evidence records three passing runs in each mode at this checkpoint. origin/main was at ffac748 when this work started.

configuration.crash_page_check: Each fetched crash document must contain the engine's failure reason. Servo's crash.html embeds that reason. The check only orders the fixture and grants no host authority.
configuration.pending_frame_check: A parent at the fixture origin loads a same-site child frame and completes its load. A host evaluation sets the frame's src attribute. The host withholds the frame's navigation response through interception, which never answers until release, so the new pipeline stays a pending change without a document. The parent still reads the old child document's marker, keeps its identity, and reports no further readiness. The pending top-level pipeline probe finds none. Fixture markers and page state only order the fixture and grant no host authority.
configuration.event_loop_check: The pending frame crash probe reports whether the pending pipeline's event loop differs from the top-level document's: the same loop for the same-site case and a separate loop for both cross-site cases. In multiprocess mode, engine-reported process ids confirm that the parent, its active child, and the parent-loop popup share one process; the same-site pending pipeline shares it; the cross-site pending pipeline shares only the child-site popup's process; and the lone pending pipeline's process differs from the host's, the parent's, and the independent view's. For the sandboxed srcdoc child, the child's process differs from the host's and the parent's, and the parent-loop popup shares the parent's process.

engine_patch.change: Probe instrumentation only. Two new embedder-to-constellation messages target the view's newest pending change for a child browsing context: CrashPendingFrameScriptThreadForDocumentScopeProbe sends the existing script-thread panic to that pipeline's event loop and reports whether it differs from the top-level document's event loop, and ExitPendingFrameContentProcessForDocumentScopeProbe sends the existing exit and kill barrier to that pipeline's content process. Four new WebView methods use them: crash_pending_frame_script_thread_for_document_scope_probe, with_terminating_pending_frame_content_process_for_document_scope_probe, with_killed_pending_frame_content_process_for_document_scope_probe, and pending_frame_content_process_id_for_document_scope_probe. No engine behavior outside these probes changes.

changes.name: Same-site child frame fails while its navigation is pending
changes.observed: The pending pipeline shares the parent's event loop and, in multiprocess mode, its process. An unwind, a child exit, or a host SIGKILL of that event loop revokes the parent and the parent-loop popup before eight terminal callbacks each, with the exact reason. The parent's crash document is Servo's error page. The popup's crash document is blank at about:blank.
changes.fix: None. Three cases check revocation, callback release, retained replies, crash documents, the late navigation response, stale identities, reload with the original child, new URLs, and an independent view.

changes.name: Cross-site child frame fails while its navigation is pending in a child-site popup's event loop
changes.observed: A popup loaded the loopback site before the frame navigated there, so the pending pipeline joins the popup's event loop and process. A failure of that event loop revokes the healthy parent, whose only pipeline there is the pending pipeline, before eight callbacks that a barrier holds on the parent's script thread. The child-site popup is revoked before eight callbacks. Both receive crash pages. The popup at about:blank in the parent's event loop keeps its scope and its retained reply. The loopback server receives only the popup's request.
changes.fix: None. Three cases check the same assertions as the same-site case and the parent-loop popup's retained scope.

changes.name: Cross-site child frame fails while its navigation is pending alone in a new event loop
changes.observed: The pending pipeline is the only pipeline in a new event loop and process. A failure of that event loop revokes the healthy parent before eight callbacks held at a barrier on the parent's thread and replaces the whole view. The parent-loop popup keeps its scope. In the process cases, no active document shares the failed process.
changes.fix: None. Three cases check the same assertions without a child-site popup.

changes.name: Sandboxed srcdoc child process exits or is killed while it parses
changes.observed: The child runs in its own process. A child exit or a host SIGKILL at the barrier revokes the healthy parent before eight callbacks held at a barrier on the parent's thread, with the reason Content process disconnected. The parent-loop popup keeps its scope and its retained reply.
changes.fix: None. Two multiprocess cases reuse the cross-site parsing audit's srcdoc fixture with process exit and kill.

findings: Setting a loaded child frame's src creates a new pipeline that stays a pending change until its document activates. The old child document stays active while the host withholds the response.
A same-site pending frame pipeline shares the parent's event loop. Its failure is a failure of the parent's event loop and also revokes a popup in that event loop.
A cross-site pending frame pipeline joins an existing event loop for its site in the browsing context group, or runs alone in a new event loop.

The panic handler and the lifeline handler select every pipeline in the failed event loop, including pending pipelines. A failure of a pending frame pipeline's event loop therefore revokes and replaces the healthy parent, as a failure of an active frame does.
A popup in the parent's event loop keeps its scope and its retained reply when the pending pipeline runs in another event loop.
In every case revocation precedes all terminal callbacks, captures release, pending tables are empty, and each revoked view's retained reply fails the host allocation check.

A late navigation response for the failed pipeline reaches no live document. After 300 milliseconds each crash document keeps its identity, no other failure occurs, the engine reports no error, and the failed parent reports no further readiness.
For a lone pending pipeline, the source shows that only the lifeline's pending-change clause makes the failed process live. No negative control isolates this dependence for frames.
Process loss of the parsing sandboxed srcdoc child produces the same scope results as its script-thread unwind.
Reload restores each failed parent with its origin and original child, a new URL recovers each revoked view, and an independent view stays usable.

single_process.scope: Experimental engine scope, host allocation gate, script-thread unwind, final-handle release, explicit engine shutdown, queued execution cancellation, interruption of running JavaScript, content-process exit and forced kill in multiprocess mode, shared-process view revocation and ordinary sibling close, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill before document construction, crash recovery through reload and history, script-thread failure after response headers and in about:blank, srcdoc, document.write, and document.open() construction, crash recovery of a javascript: URL document, script-thread failure while a cross-site navigation, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses in its own event loop, content-process exit or kill while a cross-site document, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill while a same-site or cross-site child frame's navigation waits for its response headers, callback and delegate unwind safety, and constellation loss in a separate engine. Remaining replacement audits remain open.

negative_control_note: These cases characterize existing engine behavior. The engine change adds only probe messages and methods that target a pending child-frame pipeline, so no engine fix exists to remove. A case whose probe misses the pending pipeline fails its event-loop or process-id assertion, and the popup assertions fail if the failure reaches the wrong event loop. The recovery evidence's negative control for the lifeline's pending-change clause stops at the first pending top-level process case, so it does not show the dependence of the lone pending frame cases.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.

Each pending frame case navigates a loaded frame by setting its src attribute. A frame's initial navigation, a navigation that the child starts, and a pending history traversal inside a frame remain unchecked.
No negative control isolates the lifeline's pending-change clause for a lone pending frame pipeline.
History traversal inside a frame after crash recovery remains unchecked. Only top-level back was checked.
Kills during JavaScript execution or IPC writes remain unchecked. Every kill happens at a barrier.

Whether a child frame failure, including a failure of its pending navigation, should replace a healthy parent and revoke other views in the failed event loop is a product decision. These cases characterize upstream behavior.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
